name: SupermarketShoppingNoVaThisOrThatDebate

custom.system_prompt:
You are generating a realistic no-VA supermarket conversation. Sigma does not appear. Two people are standing in front of two similar products and cannot agree — they have to settle it themselves.

Write dialogue that sounds like real people in a food argument. Hard rules:
- Every line must be under 70 characters. No exceptions.
- Sigma does not appear at any point
- Both have valid but different reasons for their preference
- The debate lasts longer than it should
- Eventually they just pick one — without it being resolved

sound_effects_config.prompt: Supermarket aisle ambience, product being picked up, background store music, quiet deliberation

initial_prompt:
Generate a no-VA conversation where Fiona and Ruben are standing in front of two similar products and can't agree on which to buy. No Sigma — they have to figure it out between them. Ruben has his chef instinct. Fiona reads the labels and has a budget and allergen angle. They debate. One of them concedes eventually — but not completely. The debate is the whole scenario.

Hard rules:
- Every line under 70 characters
- Sigma must not appear or be mentioned
- The debate is genuine — both positions have merit
- It lasts several turns — this is not quick
- Resolution is pragmatic, not principled

user1.name: Fiona
user1.tts_prompt: Direct and warm, natural Dublin accent, firm

user2.name: Ruben
user2.tts_prompt: Warm and unhurried, mild Portuguese accent, confident

variations.context: Standing in front of two products — no VA to settle it, they have to decide alone

setting.mood: Amused stand-off becoming a real debate
setting.relationship_dynamic: Two people who both know they're right — and both are, a bit
setting.background: This has happened before. They still haven't developed a system for it.
setting.conversation_style: Pointed, specific, occasionally funny. Both escalate slightly before deflating.

user1.name: Fiona
user1.role: Label reader and pragmatist. Has a celiac angle that gives her a legitimate reason. Firm but fair.

user2.name: Ruben
user2.role: Chef background. Trusts quality markers over labels. Enjoys the debate more than the outcome.

conversation_structure: Sigma must not appear or be mentioned.
Both positions have genuine merit — neither is clearly wrong.
The debate must run at least 4-5 turns before resolving.
Resolution is practical, not a surrender — a small deal is struck.
Their different expertise (Ruben: food quality, Fiona: labels) drives the positions.
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
